name: Racquet
guidance: Aluminum is fine while you decide if the sport sticks; graphite once it has.
freeAlternative: Many clubs and public courts lend a racquet for a first session.

name: Tennis balls
guidance: A fresh can bounces predictably. Old balls are fine for wall practice.
freeAlternative: Whoever you hit with usually has some.

name: Court shoes
guidance: Court soles grip and protect ankles on lateral moves. Worth it once you play regularly.
freeAlternative: Running shoes work for your first few sessions.

name: Hat and sunscreen
guidance: Outdoor courts reflect a lot of sun. Protect yourself before comfort items.

name: Overgrips
guidance: A fresh grip stops the racquet slipping. Add one once the original wears.

name: Helmet
guidance: Buy new and buy for fit. A helmet that has taken one impact is done, even if it looks fine.

name: Bike (fixed or single speed)
guidance: Fit and working brakes matter more than weight or looks. Have a shop check a used bike.
freeAlternative: A used track bike, or converting an old steel road frame, is the cheapest honest path.

name: Front brake
guidance: Required for road riding on this path, including fixed gear, whatever your skid skills.
freeAlternative: Included on most complete bikes; about $25–60 to add if yours has none.

name: U-lock
guidance: A bike without a good lock is a bike on borrowed time. Lock the frame, not just a wheel.

name: Front and rear lights
guidance: Needed from dusk onward and on grey days. Be seen from the front and behind.

name: Multi-tool, pump and spare tube
guidance: Enough to fix a flat by the road. Learn the fix at home first.
freeAlternative: Most shops will lend a floor pump.

name: Swimsuit
guidance: Anything snug that your pool accepts. Loose clothing drags and can be unsafe.
freeAlternative: Any snug athletic swimwear you already own.

name: Goggles
guidance: Fit is everything: they should seal lightly without a strap. Not something to share.

name: Pool access
guidance: Choose a pool with lifeguards. Cost varies a lot by area; campus and city pools are often cheapest.
freeAlternative: Campus rec centers and many municipal pools are free or included.

name: Swim cap
guidance: Keeps hair out of your face and the filters. Many pools require one.

name: Towel
guidance: The one you already own is perfect.
freeAlternative: One you own.

name: Fins, pull buoy or kickboard
guidance: Training tools for later. Ask your instructor before using them.
freeAlternative: Most pools have a shared bin.

name: Notebook
guidance: Anything you are not afraid to write badly in. Cheap makes it easier to start.
freeAlternative: Any notebook you own, loose paper, or a free notes app.

name: Pen
guidance: Whatever writes smoothly for you.
freeAlternative: Any pen in the house.

name: CPU
guidance: Match the socket to the motherboard exactly. One generation back is the usual value pick.

name: Motherboard
guidance: Check the socket and memory generation before anything else.

name: Memory (16–32 GB)
guidance: Match the generation the board accepts. Prices are unusually high right now; check before buying.

name: Graphics card
guidance: Only needed for games and heavy visual work. A processor with integrated graphics can skip this at first.
freeAlternative: $0 if your processor has integrated graphics.

name: Storage (1 TB NVMe)
guidance: One solid-state drive is enough to start.

name: Power supply
guidance: Buy this new and leave headroom over what the parts draw. Never the place to cut, and never open one.

name: Case
guidance: Check cooler height and card length against its specification before buying.

name: Operating system
guidance: Linux is free, and many students can get Windows through their school.
freeAlternative: Linux is free; student licenses often are too.

name: #2 Phillips screwdriver
guidance: One magnetic screwdriver does the whole build.
freeAlternative: Almost certainly one in the house already.

name: Anti-static strap
guidance: Makes it harder to forget to ground yourself.
freeAlternative: Touch the bare metal case with the power supply switched off, and avoid carpet.

name: Pencil or graphite set
guidance: Any pencil works. Harder grades smudge less, softer ones shade faster.
freeAlternative: Any pencil you own.

name: Paper or sketchbook
guidance: Cheap paper keeps you from being precious about mistakes, and volume is what teaches.
freeAlternative: Printer paper, which is what Drawabox itself recommends.

name: Eraser and sharpener
guidance: A soft eraser lifts graphite without tearing cheap paper.

name: Fineliner pens (0.5 mm)
guidance: Only needed if you follow the Drawabox curriculum, which is drawn in ink.

name: Acrylic paint starter set
guidance: Student grade is fine. A red, a blue, a yellow and a white mix almost anything.

name: Brush set
guidance: A few rounds and a flat cover most of what a beginner needs.

name: Painting surface
guidance: Canvas panels or an acrylic pad. Practice on anything that takes paint.
freeAlternative: Heavy paper or primed cardboard for practice.

name: Palette
guidance: Anything flat and wipeable. Acrylic peels cleanly off a lid.
freeAlternative: A paper plate or plastic lid.

name: Water jar and rag
guidance: Change the water more often than feels necessary.
freeAlternative: Any jar and an old shirt.

name: Running shoes
guidance: Fit matters more than model or price. A shop that watches you walk is worth the trip. Not something to buy used.
freeAlternative: Any athletic shoe you own will cover your first few weeks; replace it before your mileage builds.

name: Athletic clothes
guidance: Whatever you already exercise in.
freeAlternative: Whatever you already exercise in.

name: Moisture-wicking socks
guidance: Cotton holds sweat and causes blisters on longer runs.

name: Water bottle
guidance: Needed in heat and on longer runs, or plan a route past water.
freeAlternative: One you own.

name: Reflective vest or headlamp
guidance: Needed for low light, not optional there.
freeAlternative: Run in daylight.

name: Indoor volleyball
guidance: Sessions almost always provide balls; your own helps solo wall practice.
freeAlternative: Every gym, rec league and pickup group has balls.

name: Knee pads
guidance: Cheap, and the floor is unforgiving. Unnecessary on sand.

name: Court shoes
guidance: Indoor courts need clean non-marking soles. Court shoes add ankle support for lateral moves.
freeAlternative: Any clean non-marking athletic shoe for your first sessions.

name: Ankle braces
guidance: Worth considering if you have a history of rolling an ankle.

name: Ball pump
guidance: Only needed once you own a ball.

name: Library card
guidance: Free at any US public library with proof of address. This is your whole starting kit.
freeAlternative: Libby gives you ebooks and audiobooks on the same card, from your phone.

name: A book
guidance: Start with something you want to read, not something you think you should.
freeAlternative: The library, Libby, Project Gutenberg or a Little Free Library.

name: Book light
guidance: Light on the page rather than behind it.
freeAlternative: Any lamp.
